content.title: Cavaliers vs. Bulls: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/19/26)
content.text: The Cleveland Cavaliers (42–27) face the Chicago Bulls (28–41) tonight at the United Center in Chicago. Cleveland enters after a 123–116 road win over the shorthanded Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday. Evan Mobley and James Harden led with 27 points apiece, while Donovan Mitchell followed with 19. Mitchell is questionable for tonight’s game with a left eye contusion. After a seven-game winning streak, the Cavs have gone 6–6, stopping their surge tot het op of the Eastern Conference. Still, they maintain a 2.5-game lead over the Toronto Raptors for fourth place in the Eastern Conference. The Bulls, meanwhile, come in off a 139–109 blowout loss to the Toronto Raptors last night. Toronto overwhelmed Chicago with its offensive balance, with six players scoring 17 or more, led by RJ Barrett with 23. Josh Giddey finished with just 9 points and three assists, cooling off after posting triple-doubles in five out of his seven previous games — just falling short in the other two matchups. Matas Buzelis led with 19 points — a bit below his 22.5 PPG average this season. The Cavs have the edge here even with Mitchell sidelined. The Bulls’ offense had been clicking until last night’s loss, and could return to form. But their defense remains an issue. Prediction: Cleveland Cavaliers 123, Chicago Bulls 112 Injury Report Cleveland Cavaliers Donovan Mitchell — Day-To-Day (Eye) Olivier Sarr — Day-To-Day (Not injury related) Tyrese Proctor — Out (Quadriceps) Craig Porter Jr. — Out (Groin) Jarrett Allen — Out (Knee) Chicago Bulls Jalen Smith — Day-To-Day (Calf) Collin Sexton — Day-To-Day (Fibula) Isaac Okoro — Out (Knee) Jaden Ivey — Out (Knee) Anfernee Simons — Out (Wrist) Zach Collins — Out (Toe) Noa Essengue — Out (Shoulder) How to Watch Cavaliers vs. Bulls Tip-off for tonight’s Cavaliers-Bulls game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern / 6:00 PM Central at the United Center in Chicago. The game airs live locally on CHSN and FanDuel Sports Network Ohio. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
